tasks.title: Single-source-of-truth DB trigger: auto-create verification_case on pending_review
tasks.what: Add one AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON users trigger (WHEN new.verification_status='pending_review') that idempotently inserts a verification_case (state='new') if the user has no open case (NOT EXISTS state<>'closed'). This is the invariant enforcer that closes VF-1, VF-2, VF-5 at once. transition_user (20260619500001:202) and admin_unblock_verification (20260620920000:145) both do a plain UPDATE users SET verification_status=..., and selfie/fix routes also route through transition_user — so an AFTER-UPDATE row-level trigger fires on every path. Trigger function: SECURITY DEFINER, set search_path=public,pg_temp; guard body with IF new.verification_status='pending_review' AND NOT EXISTS(select 1 from verification_cases where user_id=new.id and state<>'closed') THEN insert into verification_cases(user_id,state) values(new.id,'new'); END IF; RETURN new. Use a WHEN clause on the trigger to skip non-pending rows cheaply. Must NOT resurrect closed cases (a fresh approve/reject sets verification_status to verified/rejected, so WHEN never fires there) and must NOT double-insert when an open case already exists (needs_changes→fix cycle: case was closed by admin_reject, user goes back to pending_review with zero open cases → trigger correctly creates a new open case). Keep created_at default now(); do not set verification_submitted_at here.
tasks.acceptance: After migration: (1) UPDATE users SET verification_status='pending_review' for a user with no open case creates exactly one verification_cases row state='new'; (2) repeating the UPDATE (or a second pending_review transition) creates NO additional case (idempotent via NOT EXISTS); (3) admin_reject(needs_changes) closes the case, then a subsequent transition to pending_review via fix/route creates a new open case; (4) approve→verified and reject→rejected transitions create no case; (5) trigger is a no-op for any UPDATE that does not set verification_status='pending_review'. Verify with a psql script running all 5 scenarios.
tasks.db_changes: New migration: CREATE FUNCTION verification_case_autocreate() + CREATE TRIGGER users_verification_case_autocreate AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF verification_status ON users FOR EACH ROW WHEN (new.verification_status='pending_review') EXECUTE FUNCTION verification_case_autocreate(). No new tables/indexes (verification_cases_user_idx + verification_cases_state_idx already exist from 20260627100100).
tasks.risk: Must use SECURITY DEFINER because callers run under invoker rights (transition_user is plain; admin_unblock is security invoker) and the trigger inserts into verification_cases — confirm the executing role has insert rights, or keep DEFINER owned by table owner. Concurrency: two rapid pending_review updates could race the NOT EXISTS check and insert two cases; mitigate with a partial unique index (one open case per user) — see VER-1b note in risk. Recommend adding a partial unique index CREATE UNIQUE INDEX verification_cases_one_open_per_user ON verification_cases(user_id) WHERE state<>'closed' in the SAME migration and having the trigger swallow unique_violation, making it race-safe.

Backup cron runner: сам скрипт tar→R2 гонять как отдельный Railway scheduled job (bash) или как /api/cron/backup endpoint под X-Cron-Secret (как housekeeping). Volume single-attach смонтирован к web-инстансу → endpoint имеет доступ к /data; отдельный job — нет. Рекомендация: endpoint-путь, т.к. только web-инстанс видит /data.

TOTP: hand-roll RFC 6238 через node:crypto (паритет с существующим scrypt/HMAC-стилем, ноль новых deps) vs добавить otplib/@noble. Рекомендация: hand-roll (~40 строк HMAC-SHA1 + base32), т.к. codebase намеренно lean и crypto-native. Требует qrcode для otpauth — QR можно рендерить на клиенте (otpauth:// строку показываем + опционально client-side qr), чтобы не тянуть серверный qrcode-dep.

Recovery codes для TOTP: генерировать N одноразовых кодов при enrollment (hashed в admin_users/новой таблице) — иначе потеря телефона = перманентный lockout superadmin. Нужно решение: делать в MVP или принять риск ручного reset через SQL.

Cron reliability: остаться на GitHub Actions free-tier (best-effort, доку C3 говорит что падает) + dead-man's-switch, ИЛИ перенести на Railway scheduled jobs / cron-job.org (надёжнее). Рекомендация: Railway scheduled jobs для housekeeping+backup, GH Actions оставить только как fallback для outbox.

Alert channel: Telegram-сообщение в ops-чат через существующий Bot API (ноль новых deps, токен уже есть) vs Slack webhook vs Sentry. Рекомендация: Telegram ops-chat для крон/outbox-алертов (дёшево, MVP). OPS_ALERT_CHAT_ID в env.

Rate-limit backing store: in-memory token-bucket в proxy.ts (корректно для single-instance, реплики архитектурно невозможны из-за single-attach volume) vs Postgres (переживает рестарт/деплой, паттерн admin_login_attempts). ВЕРИФИЦИРОВАТЬ что middleware у нас runs in-process на next start (не edge-isolated) — иначе in-memory per-isolate и бесполезен. Рекомендация: in-memory для флуда + Postgres-fallback для дорогих роутов (bootstrap).

tasks.title: Constant-time сравнение webhook/cron секретов (INFRA-09)
tasks.what: Заменить прямые `got !== expected` / `provided !== cronSecret` на существующий safeEqual (src/lib/crypto/safe-equal.ts) в telegram-webhook и обоих cron-роутах. Устраняет теоретический timing-канал на секретах, приводит к тому же стандарту, что уже применён в verifyStorageSig и admin-session. Сохранить fail-closed поведение (missing secret у cron → 503 остаётся). Webhook secret_token VERIFIED уже реализован end-to-end: scripts/set-webhook.mjs передаёт secret_token в setWebhook, env.ts делает TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET REQUIRED (min 16, fail-closed на boot), route отбраковывает 401 — строить нечего, только hardening сравнения.
tasks.acceptance: Все три сравнения секретов идут через safeEqual; unit-тест: валидный секрет → проходит, невалидный (в т.ч. префикс валидного) → 401, отсутствующий заголовок → 401; cron без env CRON_SECRET → 503; webhook без TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET не стартует (env.parse бросает). Нет прямых !== на секретных строках в этих файлах (grep-проверка).
tasks.risk: safeEqual бросает на разной длине — обёрнуто внутри хелпера (сравнивает длину заранее), но проверить что got может быть null (header отсутствует): safeEqual(null-cast) → привести к строке до вызова, иначе Buffer.from(null) кинет.

tasks.title: Глобальный rate-limit (IP + session token-bucket) в middleware
tasks.what: Добавить token-bucket rate-limit в src/proxy.ts (middleware) поверх существующих CSRF/session-гардов. Ключ = trustedIp(req) (уже есть, src/lib/http/ip.ts) для анонимных + bx_session-хэш для авторизованных. Отдельные, более жёсткие ведёрки для дорогих/абьюзабельных путей: /api/auth/bootstrap (масс-регистрация), чтение профиля/feed. Per-user кулдаун на /start (bot) — в handleUpdate. Реализовать in-memory token-bucket модуль src/lib/http/rate-limit.ts (Map + refill по времени); для bootstrap продублировать в Postgres (паттерн admin_login_attempts) чтобы лимит переживал деплой. При превышении → 429 с Retry-After. ВЕРИФИЦИРОВАТЬ до реализации: middleware у нас исполняется in-process (next start на Railway, не edge-isolated) — иначе in-memory Map per-isolate и бесполезен; если edge — только Postgres-путь.
tasks.db_changes: Опц.: таблица request_rate (ip/key, bucket, window_started_at) ИЛИ переиспользовать паттерн admin_login_attempts для bootstrap-лимита. Индекс по (key, window). Мигр. в supabase/migrations/ как native SQL.
tasks.acceptance: N+1-й запрос с одного IP в окне → 429 + Retry-After (тест: цикл fetch на /api/auth/bootstrap превышает порог → 429). Легитимный трафик одного юзера (открытие app, feed, чат-поллинг 1.5с) НЕ ловит 429 при нормальном темпе. /start от одного tg_id чаще кулдауна → бот молча дедупит. Health/webhook/cron/storage-serving исключены из лимита (не ломать TG-доставку/serving). Подтверждено (лог/эксперимент), что middleware runs in-process.
tasks.risk: Chat SSE поллит БД каждые 1.5с (DBS-01) — легко пересечь наивный лимит и сломать чат; лимиты калибровать по реальному темпу поллинга, чат-поллинг вынести в щадящее ведро или исключить. TG WebView за CGNAT → много юзеров с одного IP: IP-лимит должен быть достаточно широким, точечные лимиты вешать на session-ключ.

tasks.title: Потолок body-size на upload-роутах (anti-OOM)
tasks.what: Ввести жёсткий лимит размера тела ДО полной буферизации на роутах загрузки паспорта/селфи/фото. Сейчас каждый делает `await file.arrayBuffer()` в память без cap → одиночный инстанс (2-4GB RAM, force-dynamic SSR + вся картинко-полоса) уязвим к OOM (доку: «картинки текут через Node с полной буферизацией»). В middleware отвергать по Content-Length > MAX (напр. 12MB, текущий cap) до route-handler; в самих роутах — вторая проверка размера буфера (chunked/omitted Content-Length middleware не ловит) с 413 payload_too_large до записи на volume. Вынести MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES в общий модуль.
tasks.acceptance: POST с Content-Length > MAX → 413 из middleware без чтения тела. POST без/с обманным Content-Length но телом > MAX → 413 из роута до записи в /data (тест на реальном большом буфере). Легитимное фото 1-3MB грузится как раньше. Значение MAX едино для трёх роутов (импорт из одного места).
tasks.risk: Next 16 formData()/route могут иметь свой bodyParser-лимит — согласовать, чтобы наш 413 срабатывал раньше и с понятной ошибкой, а не generic 500. Проверить, что uploadDocumentImage не начинает писать частично до проверки.

tasks.title: Cloudflare / WAF перед Railway как rate-floor (config, не код)
tasks.what: Поставить Cloudflare (или эквивалент) proxy перед прод-доменом Railway: DNS-проксирование (оранжевое облако), managed WAF ruleset, edge rate-limit как нижний барьер до того, как трафик доходит до единственного инстанса, базовая DDoS-защита. Убедиться, что trustedIp() продолжает извлекать реальный клиентский IP (CF ставит CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For — при необходимости добавить CF-Connecting-IP в приоритет src/lib/http/ip.ts). Проверить, что TG WebView и bot-webhook проходят через CF без блокировок (webhook — от серверов Telegram, не блокировать).
tasks.acceptance: Прод-домен резолвится через CF (proxied). Тестовый флуд-скрипт ловит CF edge rate-limit до Railway (проверка по CF-логам/аналитике). trustedIp() возвращает реальный клиентский IP за CF (лог admin-login IP корректен, не CF-edge-IP). Bot-webhook и mini-app открываются нормально. Изменение — уровня инфра-конфига + опц. правка приоритета заголовка в ip.ts.
tasks.risk: CF в режиме proxy может ломать TG WebView / SSE (буферизация) — проверить, что /api/chats/[id]/stream (SSE) не буферизуется CF (нужен bypass/cache-off для стрима). Неверный порядок заголовков → throttle/audit по CF-IP вместо клиента.

tasks.title: Миграция: totp_secret + enrollment-поля в admin_users
tasks.what: Native SQL-миграция (в supabase/migrations/, имя каталога легаси — стек node-pg, не Supabase): добавить в admin_users колонки totp_secret text null (base32, зашифрован-at-rest опц.), totp_enrolled_at timestamptz null. Опц. таблица admin_totp_recovery_codes (admin_id, code_hash, used_at) если решаем делать recovery (см. open_decisions). Существующая схема admin_users: id/login/role/password_hash/created_at — только ADD COLUMN, обратно-совместимо (null = не enrolled).
tasks.db_changes: ALTER TABLE admin_users ADD COLUMN totp_secret text, ADD COLUMN totp_enrolled_at timestamptz. Опц. CREATE TABLE admin_totp_recovery_codes(admin_id uuid references admin_users(id) on delete cascade, code_hash text, used_at timestamptz).
tasks.acceptance: Миграция применяется на копии прод-схемы без ошибок; существующие admin_users получают totp_secret=null (не enrolled, login-совместимость сохранена до включения enforcement). Rollback-путь задокументирован.
tasks.risk: totp_secret at-rest: если не шифровать, дамп БД раскрывает 2FA-семя. Минимум — тот же уровень защиты, что и password_hash; рассмотреть шифрование секрета ключом из env (как SESSION_SECRET-производные).

tasks.title: TOTP enrollment flow (генерация секрета, otpauth URI, verify)
tasks.what: Модуль src/lib/admin/totp.ts: RFC 6238 через node:crypto (HMAC-SHA1, 30s step, 6 цифр, ±1 окно допуска на clock-skew) — hand-roll в стиле существующего scrypt/HMAC (ноль новых deps, см. open_decisions), включая base32-энкод/декод секрета. Enrollment endpoint(ы) под admin-session: POST /api/admin/totp/enroll — генерит секрет, сохраняет как pending (не активирует), возвращает otpauth://-строку (QR рендерит клиент); POST /api/admin/totp/enroll/verify — принимает первый код, при успехе ставит totp_enrolled_at=now (активация), выдаёт recovery-коды (если решено). Мини UI-экран в /admin для enrollment. Записать в admin_audit_log (action='totp_enroll').
tasks.db_changes: Пишет в admin_users.totp_secret/totp_enrolled_at (из SEC-2a); опц. recovery-codes insert.
tasks.acceptance: Superadmin в /admin проходит enrollment: сканирует QR (otpauth URI), вводит 6-значный код из Google Authenticator → totp_enrolled_at выставлен. totp.ts verify: код из эталонного authenticator принимается, код ±1 шаг принимается, устаревший/чужой код отвергается (unit-тест против известных RFC 6238 test-vectors). Enroll-роуты требуют валидную admin-session (иначе 401). Событие в audit-log.
tasks.risk: Clock-skew: сервер и телефон должны совпадать в пределах окна — допуск ±1 шаг обязателен, иначе ложные отказы. base32: свой энкодер должен точно соответствовать RFC 4648 (иначе authenticator сгенерит другой код) — покрыть test-vectors.

tasks.title: Двухшаговый admin-login с TOTP + enforcement для superadmin
tasks.what: Расширить src/app/api/admin/login/route.ts: после успешной проверки пароля, если у админа totp_enrolled_at не null → НЕ выдавать полную admin-session, а промежуточное состояние pending_totp (подписанная короткоживущая cookie, содержит adminId+role, флаг totp_pending) и вернуть {ok:true, totp_required:true}. Новый POST /api/admin/login/totp принимает 6-значный код против totp_secret (+ recovery-код как fallback), при успехе апгрейдит до полной bx_admin-сессии (setAdminSession). Enforcement: superadmin ОБЯЗАН иметь TOTP — если totp_enrolled_at=null у superadmin, login редиректит на enrollment (не выдаёт полную сессию). Троттлинг (isLoginThrottled) распространить на totp-шаг (по adminId), чтобы не брутфорсить 6 цифр. Audit: action='login' только после прохождения TOTP.
tasks.db_changes: Читает totp_secret/totp_enrolled_at; при recovery — помечает admin_totp_recovery_codes.used_at.
tasks.acceptance: Enrolled admin: пароль-ОК → {totp_required:true}, полной bx_admin-cookie НЕТ; неверный TOTP → 401, верный → полная сессия, доступ к /admin. Superadmin без enrollment → принудительно на totp-setup, не получает доступ к паспортам. TOTP-шаг троттлится (5 неверных кодов/15мин по adminId → 429). Recovery-код одноразовый (повтор → отказ). Migration-safe: НЕ включать enforcement в прод до того, как superadmin реально прошёл SEC-2b (иначе self-lockout).
tasks.risk: Self-lockout: если enforcement выкатить до enrollment живого superadmin — никто не войдёт. Обязателен порядок: enroll на проде вручную → потом флаг enforcement. pending_totp cookie должна быть подписана (HMAC как bx_admin) и коротко жить (<5мин), иначе обход пароля.

tasks.title: Ночной зашифрованный off-site backup /data (паспорта/селфи) → R2/S3
tasks.what: Backup-эндпоинт /api/cron/backup под X-Cron-Secret (endpoint-путь, т.к. только web-инстанс видит single-attach volume /data): tar каталога STORAGE_DIR (/data) → шифрование (age/gpg symmetric ключом BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY из env) → загрузка в R2/S3 бакет с датой в ключе, ротация (хранить N дней). Логировать размер/кол-во файлов/длительность. Триггер — Railway scheduled job / cron-job.org (см. SEC-4a) раз в сутки. НЕ класть ключ шифрования только в env без оффлайн-копии (см. open_decisions — иначе backup нерасшифруем при потере env).
tasks.acceptance: Вызов эндпоинта с валидным X-Cron-Secret → в R2/S3 появляется зашифрованный tar с датой, содержащий полный срез /data (кол-во объектов совпадает с list). Без секрета → 401/503 (constant-time, как SEC-5). Ключ шифрования и его оффлайн-копия задокументированы. env расширен BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY + R2/S3-креды (fail-closed валидация).
tasks.risk: tar большого /data (30-90GB на масштабе) в одном запросе может упереться в память/таймаут инстанса — стримить tar напрямую в upload (multipart), не буферизовать; на MVP-объёме ок, но заложить стриминг. Backup конкурирует за тот же диск/CPU что и живой трафик — гонять ночью.

Кода почти нет — конфиг + запись RPO/RTO в runbook.
tasks.db_changes: Railway managed Postgres auto-backup (dashboard toggle), не SQL-миграция.
tasks.acceptance: Скриншот/подтверждение: /data помечен persistent volume; Railway Postgres auto-backup включён с заданной ретенцией; в доке зафиксированы RPO (макс. потеря данных) и RTO (время восстановления) для БД. Не 'greenlit' — реально включено.

tasks.title: Провести реальный restore-тест (БД + volume) и задокументировать RPO/RTO
tasks.what: ПРОВЕСТИ, не описать: восстановить (a) Railway Postgres-снапшот в отдельную БД и убедиться, что схема+данные целы; (b) скачать последний зашифрованный volume-backup из R2/S3, расшифровать ключом, распаковать во временный каталог и проверить, что паспорта/селфи читаются (кол-во+хэши совпадают с оригиналом, случайная выборка открывается). Зафиксировать фактические RPO/RTO по таймингу и краткий restore-runbook (шаги, где ключ, кого звать).
tasks.acceptance: Restore ФАКТИЧЕСКИ выполнен: (a) БД-снапшот развёрнут, выборочные строки users/admin_users присутствуют; (b) volume-backup расшифрован и распакован, sha256 случайной выборки файлов совпадает с оригиналом на /data, файлы открываются как валидные изображения. В доке — измеренные RPO/RTO и пошаговый runbook. Acceptance НЕ 'скрипт существует', а 'restore проведён и верифицирован'.

tasks.title: Надёжно планировать housekeeping-cron (SLA reclaim сейчас фиктивен)
tasks.what: /api/cron/housekeeping (gc_start_token_uses + admin_sla_reclaim_stale_cases) НИЧЕМ не планируется — в railway.json нет cron-поля, GH Actions гонит только tg-outbox. => 7-дневный SLA-reclaim брошенных verification-кейсов не выполняется никогда (Кластер F/C3). Добавить надёжный планировщик: Railway scheduled job (или cron-job.org) на POST /api/cron/housekeeping раз в час с X-Cron-Secret; аналогично запланировать SEC-1a backup (раз в сутки). GH Actions free-tier оставить максимум как fallback для outbox (доку: падает на free-tier). Idem-потентность RPC уже обеспечена.
tasks.acceptance: housekeeping вызывается по расписанию (лог/аудит показывает регулярные вызовы каждый час); стейл verification-кейс старше 7д реально возвращается в очередь (проверка на тестовом кейсе). backup-cron (SEC-1a) запланирован раз в сутки. Планировщик — не GH free-tier для критичных задач.
tasks.risk: Railway scheduled jobs исполняются в отдельном контейнере без доступа к volume — для backup (нужен /data) использовать HTTP-триггер на web-инстанс (endpoint-путь SEC-1a), а не job с прямым доступом к диску.

tasks.title: Алерты на сбой крона, застой outbox и mass admin-login-throttle
tasks.what: Alert-path (сейчас его нет — только console.error в эфемерный stdout). Дёшево: Telegram-сообщение в ops-чат через существующий Bot API (ноль новых deps, токен есть), OPS_ALERT_CHAT_ID в env. Триггеры: (1) любой cron-вызов вернул ok:false / 5xx / не вызывался в срок (dead-man's-switch — cron-job.org или Railway healthcheck на факт исполнения); (2) глубина tg_outbox (pending) выше порога ИЛИ есть строки attempts>=5 (застряли, processOutboxBatch их скипает навсегда) — проверять в housekeeping и алертить; (3) всплеск admin-login-throttle (сигнал credential-stuffing) — при recordLoginAttempt/throttle. Модуль src/lib/ops/alert.ts (sendOpsAlert). Мини restore/oncall-runbook: кого будить если очередь встала / крон сдох / админ залочен / mass-ban.
tasks.db_changes: SELECT count по tg_outbox WHERE sent_at is null и WHERE attempts>=5 (индекс tg_outbox_unsent_idx уже есть). Опц. RPC outbox_health().
tasks.acceptance: Симуляция: cron-роут возвращает ok:false → приходит Telegram-алерт в ops-чат. Инъекция N pending / строки с attempts>=5 в tg_outbox → housekeeping шлёт алерт о застое. >K неудачных admin-login с разных ключей в окне → алерт credential-stuffing. Алерты дедуплицируются (не спамят каждую минуту). Runbook описывает реакцию на каждый алерт.
tasks.risk: sendOpsAlert через Bot API сам может упасть/зашуметь — не блокировать основной путь (try/catch, best-effort, как adminAudit в login-роуте) и вводить cooldown, иначе шторм алертов при длительном инциденте. Застрявшие attempts>=5 строки нужен ещё и ручной reset (attempts=0) — упомянуть в runbook.

plans.goal: The system survives launch-scale concurrency (hundreds of open chats, /main opens, cron) on Railway single-attach Postgres without exhausting DB connections or degrading unrelated routes. Concretely: (1) connection pooling via PgBouncer transaction-mode with an explicit, sized app pool; (2) the live-chat SSE stream no longer polls the DB every 1.5s — idle DB-connection count is independent of the number of open SSE streams; (3) the hot recommendation path and per-SSE-tick chat reads are index-backed; (4) get_recommendations no longer silently drops the true top match nor masks scan timeouts as "no candidates"; (5) an EXPLAIN ANALYZE harness on a 10k-row seed proves index scans before launch. Addresses launch-readiness IDs DBS-01..DBS-08, INFRA-09, INFRA-10.
plans.sequencing_note: Two independent tracks that can run in parallel: (A) connection/SSE track VER... no — use these IDs: DB-1 (PgBouncer + pool) and DB-2/DB-3 (LISTEN/NOTIFY SSE) form the connection track; DB-4/DB-5/DB-6 (indexes, sargable rewrite, RPC correctness) form the query track; DB-7 (10k seed) then DB-8 (EXPLAIN harness) verify the query track. Recommended order: land DB-1 first (unblocks safe pooling and is the single biggest fix, DBS-01). In parallel start DB-4 (indexes) and DB-7 (seed) since they have no code deps. DB-2/DB-3 (SSE rewrite) is the largest single item and can proceed independently of the query track. DB-5 and DB-6 depend on DB-4 (indexes) and DB-7 (seed) for their acceptance. DB-8 depends on DB-4/DB-5/DB-6 landing and DB-7 seed. CRITICAL cross-cutting: DB-1's PgBouncer transaction-mode forces two design constraints that must be honored by other tasks — (a) DB-3's listener must use a DIRECT (non-pooled, 5432) connection, and (b) pool.ts startup GUCs (statement_timeout etc.) must move off the connection-startup `options` string to ALTER ROLE / per-txn SET or they are dropped by the pooler. Both are called out in the respective tasks.
open_decisions: DBS-04 (silent best-match loss): scoring lives in JS (src/lib/matching/score.ts), so NO SQL pre-ORDER-BY short of moving the score into SQL can guarantee the true top-1 survives a LIMIT truncation. Two honest options for MVP: (a) score ALL viable candidates in JS by raising p_limit high / removing the LIMIT (the hard filters — mutual gender + age window + published + >=1 approved photo — likely reduce the viable set to low hundreds per viewer, not 10k, so this is cheap); or (b) port scoreCandidate() into the SQL RPC and ORDER BY score in-DB. DB-6 assumes option (a) as the MVP default; confirm with founder whether the viable-set size makes (a) safe or (b) is warranted. Verify actual viable-set size on the 10k seed (DB-7/DB-8) before committing.

PgBouncer hosting: run PgBouncer as a separate Railway service/sidecar vs. Railway's managed pooler if offered. Affects DB-1 wiring (two URLs: pooled 6543 + direct 5432) and whether the direct URL for DB-3 is even reachable from the app network. Confirm Railway topology.

LISTEN/NOTIFY vs Redis pub/sub for DB-2/DB-3: plan assumes Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY (no new infra, 0 idle DB cost with a shared listener). If a Redis instance is already provisioned for other reasons, pub/sub is marginally simpler operationally. Default: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY.

NOTIFY delivery mechanism for DB-2: DB trigger on chat_messages/chats (fires atomically on commit, covers all write paths) vs. app-level pg_notify calls in the 3 routes. Plan defaults to triggers for atomicity/robustness; app-level is acceptable if trigger maintenance is judged too heavy.

Typing signal over NOTIFY: typing_*_until is ephemeral (6s TTL) and currently piggybacks on the chat row. Decide whether typing warrants a NOTIFY channel at all or whether the client can keep a lightweight local optimistic indicator — affects DB-2 scope (whether the /typing route/chats trigger emits).

tasks.title: PgBouncer (transaction-mode) + explicit sized app pool + relocate startup GUCs
tasks.what: Introduce PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode in front of Railway Postgres and point the app pool at it. Add a second env var for the DIRECT (non-pooled, 5432) connection used only by the LISTEN listener (DB-3) and by migrations. In src/lib/env.ts add DATABASE_URL (pooled, 6543) and a new DATABASE_DIRECT_URL (direct, 5432) plus optional PG_POOL_MAX (already read from process.env in pool.ts but undocumented). In src/lib/db/pool.ts: set an explicit `max` derived from PG_POOL_MAX with a sane default (e.g. 15) sized against Postgres max_connections and the pooler's pool_size; CRITICAL — REMOVE the `-c statement_timeout=... -c idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=... -c application_name=...` from the pg `options` startup string, because PgBouncer transaction mode drops/rejects startup GUCs, and instead apply these via `ALTER ROLE <app_user> SET statement_timeout='10000'` etc. (new migration) or per-transaction SET. Document the two URLs and pooler settings in .env.local.example and CLAUDE.md. Update README migration command to use DATABASE_DIRECT_URL.
tasks.acceptance: With PgBouncer transaction-mode in front, N concurrent app requests do not open more than PG_POOL_MAX backend connections to Postgres (verify via pg_stat_activity count by application_name under a concurrency test). statement_timeout=10s and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=60s are observably in effect on pooled connections (SHOW statement_timeout returns 10s inside an app query) despite the options string being removed. A forgotten/slow query is still killed at 10s. DATABASE_DIRECT_URL is present and reaches Postgres bypassing the pooler.
tasks.db_changes: New migration ALTER ROLE <app_user> SET statement_timeout, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, application_name (replaces the connection-startup options that transaction-mode PgBouncer drops).
tasks.risk: Transaction-mode PgBouncer silently drops session-level features; must confirm every code path is transaction-scoped (no session-pinned LISTEN, no session GUCs relied upon). prepared-statement/portal issues with node-pg under transaction pooling — verify pg queries don't rely on server-side prepared statements across pooled txns.

tasks.title: Add commit-atomic NOTIFY on chat message insert, read-receipt update, and typing
tasks.what: Emit Postgres NOTIFY on a per-chat channel so instances can push live updates without polling. Preferred (default): a DB trigger AFTER INSERT ON chat_messages and AFTER UPDATE OF read_at ON chat_messages that calls pg_notify('chat_<chat_id>' or a single 'chat_events' channel with chat_id in payload) with a compact JSON payload (kind: 'message'|'read', chat_id, and minimal fields); plus a trigger AFTER UPDATE OF typing_a_until/typing_b_until ON chats emitting kind:'typing'. This covers all three SSE payload dimensions ({messages, read_through, typing}) and all write paths — including the app routes messages/route.ts (insert at line 85), read/route.ts (bulk read_at update, lines 24-29), typing/route.ts (chats update, line 28) — atomically on commit. Keep payloads small (IDs + kind), not full rows, to avoid the 8000-byte NOTIFY limit; the SSE stream re-reads the specific changed data via existing getLiveState on wake.
tasks.acceptance: Inserting a chat_messages row, updating read_at, or updating typing_*_until each produces exactly one NOTIFY on the chat channel with a payload under 8000 bytes containing chat_id and kind. A LISTEN'ing psql session receives all three event kinds. Direct (non-route) inserts into chat_messages also notify (trigger, not app-level).
tasks.db_changes: New migration: pg_notify triggers on chat_messages (AFTER INSERT, AFTER UPDATE OF read_at) and chats (AFTER UPDATE OF typing_a_until, typing_b_until). Channel naming + payload shape defined here.
tasks.risk: NOTIFY 8KB payload cap — must send IDs/kind only, not message bodies. Bulk read_at update in /read touches many rows; use a statement-level trigger (or dedupe) so one /read call emits one NOTIFY, not one-per-row.

tasks.title: Rewrite SSE stream: shared per-process LISTEN listener + in-process fan-out (remove 1.5s DB polling)
tasks.what: Replace the 1.5s DB-polling loop in src/app/api/chats/[id]/stream/route.ts with an event-driven model. Create a single process-wide listener module (e.g. src/lib/chat/notify-listener.ts) that opens ONE dedicated pg Client on DATABASE_DIRECT_URL (NOT the pooled URL and NOT from the pool — transaction-mode PgBouncer cannot hold a session LISTEN), issues LISTEN once for the chat_events channel, and fans out incoming notifications to in-process SSE subscribers via an EventEmitter keyed by chat_id. The stream route subscribes to its chat_id, and on each relevant NOTIFY calls the existing getLiveState(id, user.id, chat, cursor) once to fetch just the delta, then pushes the SSE frame. Keep heartbeat pings and the MAX_MS early-close. Keep loadChatRow's block-check on subscribe and re-check on receipt so blocked streams still tear down. The existing client fallback polling in ChatRoom.tsx (EventSource onerror → FALLBACK_POLL_MS) stays as-is (no change needed) as a safety net. Result: at rest, zero DB queries per open SSE stream; DB is touched only when a real event fires.
tasks.acceptance: With K open SSE streams and no chat activity, the number of Postgres backends attributable to SSE is exactly 1 per app instance (the shared listener), independent of K — verified via pg_stat_activity. A new message / read / typing event reaches the correct stream(s) within ~1s without any per-tick polling query. The shared listener auto-reconnects (re-LISTENs) on connection drop. Blocked pair: stream tears down on next event or heartbeat. Client still works if EventSource fails (fallback poll path unchanged).
tasks.db_changes: None (consumes DB-2 channel).
tasks.risk: Serverless/multi-instance: NOTIFY reaches every instance's listener backend, so fan-out is correct across instances; but a per-request LISTEN (the wrong design) would recreate connection exhaustion — the listener MUST be a single shared connection. Next.js module singleton lifetime across route invocations must be verified (module-level singleton, guarded init). Listener must use direct 5432 URL, never the pooler.

tasks.title: Add missing hot-path indexes (approved photos, unread messages)
tasks.what: Add the two partial indexes flagged INFRA-10 and DBS-07. (1) profile_photos partial index supporting the correlated approved-photo lookup and EXISTS in get_recommendations: `CREATE INDEX profile_photos_approved_idx ON profile_photos (user_id, is_main DESC, ord) WHERE status='approved'` (covers both the EXISTS filter and the ORDER BY is_main desc, ord LIMIT 1 subselect at recommendations RPC lines 30-32/45). (2) chat_messages partial unread index for the per-SSE-tick / per-send read-through and unread scans: `CREATE INDEX chat_messages_unread_idx ON chat_messages (chat_id, sender_id) WHERE read_at IS NULL` (serves getLiveState read_through query in live.ts:68-76, the unreadFromMe count in messages/route.ts:75-80, and the /read update predicate). Keep the existing chat_messages(chat_id, created_at) for the message-window scan.
tasks.acceptance: After migration, EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a 10k seed shows the approved-photo subselect/EXISTS in get_recommendations uses profile_photos_approved_idx (Index Scan/Index Only Scan, not Seq Scan), and the read_through/unread queries use chat_messages_unread_idx. No duplicate/unused index warnings.
tasks.db_changes: New migration: two partial indexes (profile_photos WHERE status='approved'; chat_messages WHERE read_at IS NULL).
tasks.risk: CREATE INDEX locks; use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY if run against a live DB with data (note: CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside the concatenated-migration transaction — may need to run this migration standalone). Partial-index predicate must exactly match query predicates or the planner won't use it.

tasks.title: Make get_recommendations age filter sargable (birth_date BETWEEN) + covering index
tasks.what: Rewrite the two non-sargable age predicates in the latest get_recommendations RPC (current def: supabase/migrations/20260630000000_recommendations_v3_top_life_values.sql, lines 43-44) from `date_part('year', age(cp.birth_date))::int BETWEEN v.partner_age_min AND v.partner_age_max` to a sargable birth_date range: candidate born between (current_date - (max_age+1) years + 1 day) and (current_date - min_age years), i.e. compute date bounds from the viewer's partner_age_min/max and compare cp.birth_date directly. Mirror the reverse predicate (v.age between cp.partner_age_min and cp.partner_age_max) — this side is on the viewer's own age vs candidate window; keep it correct but note it's a scalar comparison, not the hot scan. Add a supporting index on user_profiles enabling the candidate scan by the hard filters, e.g. `CREATE INDEX user_profiles_reco_idx ON user_profiles (looking_for_gender, gender, status, birth_date) WHERE status='published'` (order tuned to the mutual-gender + published + birth_date-range access pattern). CAUTION: the bound inversion — a HIGHER max age maps to an EARLIER birth_date — and age() truncation vs date-arithmetic birthday edges must be handled so the rewritten predicate returns the identical candidate set.
tasks.acceptance: On the 10k seed, the rewritten RPC returns the EXACT SAME candidate set (same user_ids) as the current date_part(age()) version for a battery of viewers spanning age-window edges and birthday-boundary dates (assert set equality, not just row count). EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows an Index Scan on user_profiles using user_profiles_reco_idx (or the birth_date range), NOT a Seq Scan over all profiles. recommend.ts still consumes the same return columns (no signature change).
tasks.db_changes: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_recommendations with sargable birth_date bounds; new supporting index on user_profiles. Preserves return-table shape (vals=top_life_values) for recommend.ts/score.ts compat.
tasks.risk: Off-by-one / bound inversion / birthday-edge mismatch vs age() truncation is the whole risk — acceptance is set-equality on the seed, not 'looks indexed'. Keep the RPC return columns byte-compatible with recommend.ts.

tasks.title: Fix silent best-match loss (DBS-04) and timeout-masked-as-empty (DBS-08)
tasks.what: Two correctness fixes around the LIMIT. (1) DBS-04: the RPC currently `LIMIT p_limit` (called with 100 from recommend.ts:39) with NO ORDER BY, so once >100 candidates match, the JS scorer (score.ts) never sees the true top-1. Since the score is JS-side, adopt the open-decision default (option a): raise/remove the LIMIT so ALL viable candidates (post hard-filter) are scored in JS — verify on the seed that the viable set is bounded (low hundreds) so this is safe; if the seed shows it can blow past a safe ceiling, escalate to porting score into SQL (option b) per open_decisions. Update recommend.ts p_limit accordingly and document why. (2) DBS-08: getRecommendations currently swallows RPC error and returns [] (recommend.ts:41 `if (error || !rows) return []`), so a statement_timeout kill under load is indistinguishable from a genuine empty result and surfaces as 'алгоритм ищет'. Distinguish: on a query error/timeout, log + surface a distinct signal (throw or return a typed error) so match-of-the-day / UI can show a retry state rather than the permanent empty state, and so timeouts are observable.
tasks.acceptance: On the 10k seed, for a viewer with >100 matching candidates, the candidate ultimately shown (top by score.ts) is provably the global max score across ALL viable candidates, not just among the first 100 returned (test asserts this against a brute-force JS scoring of the full filtered set). A forced statement_timeout / RPC error produces a distinct error signal (logged + typed) — NOT a silent empty array indistinguishable from 'no candidates'; match-of-the-day surfaces retry vs genuine-empty differently.
tasks.db_changes: Possibly none beyond DB-5 (LIMIT change is app-side if option a). Only if option b chosen: port scoreCandidate into SQL + ORDER BY score in RPC.
tasks.risk: Removing/raising the LIMIT trades correctness for scan cost — must confirm on the seed that the viable set per viewer stays bounded, else it reintroduces a heavy scan. Error-surfacing change must not break the legitimate empty-state UX.

tasks.title: 10k-row seed generator across FKs, enums, and realistic distributions
tasks.what: Build a repeatable seed script that populates ~10k users with the full graph needed to exercise the hot paths: users (lifecycle_state='active', verification_status='approved'), user_profiles (published, valid gender/looking_for_gender pairings, birth_date spanning the age windows, city distribution weighted to Tashkent per the 80/20 gender-imbalance concern, top_life_values arrays, partner_age_min/max), profile_photos (>=1 approved per active user, is_main/ord set), quiz_results vectors, plus a realistic spread of chats + chat_messages (some unread) and match_requests/match_views/blocks so the NOT EXISTS filters and unread indexes are actually exercised. Must satisfy all FK and enum/check constraints so it loads clean via the direct URL. Idempotent / re-runnable (truncate-and-reseed guard). Place under scripts/.
tasks.acceptance: Running the seed against a fresh DB (direct URL) inserts ~10k active+approved+published users each with >=1 approved photo, valid mutual-gender/age distributions, and a nontrivial chat/message/match graph, with ZERO FK/enum/check violations. Re-running is safe (idempotent). Produces enough viable candidates per sample viewer to make the LIMIT and index tests meaningful (some viewers with >100 matches).
tasks.db_changes: None (data only). Must respect all init_schema + later-migration constraints (enums onboarding_step, lifecycle/verification states, profile_photos status, etc.).
tasks.risk: Getting distributions wrong (e.g. no viewer exceeds 100 matches, or nobody passes mutual filters) makes DB-5/DB-6 acceptance vacuous. Must model the mutual gender+age constraints so pairs actually match.

tasks.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE harness proving index scans on the 10k seed
tasks.what: Create a runnable harness (script + checked-in expected results / assertions) that, against the DB-7 seed, runs EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on: get_recommendations for a spread of viewers; the getLiveState read_through query; the messages/route unread-count query; and the /read update. Assert plan shape: Index Scan/Index Only Scan on user_profiles_reco_idx, profile_photos_approved_idx, chat_messages_unread_idx — and NO Seq Scan on user_profiles / profile_photos / chat_messages on the hot paths. Capture timings as a pre-launch baseline. Wire this to run in CI or as a documented pre-launch gate.
tasks.acceptance: Harness runs green against the 10k seed: every hot query uses the intended index (assertion fails on any Seq Scan of user_profiles/profile_photos/chat_messages in the hot paths), get_recommendations p95 under a defined threshold (e.g. <50ms) on the seed, and a baseline plan+timing report is written. Re-runnable before each launch-affecting DB change.
tasks.db_changes: None (read-only EXPLAIN).
tasks.risk: EXPLAIN plans are data-dependent; must ANALYZE the seed tables first or the planner picks seq scans on stale stats and the harness reports false failures. Thresholds must reflect PgBouncer/prod-like settings, not a warm local cache.

plans.goal: Baxtlilar перестаёт быть 'слепым': unhandled-ошибки на сервере/клиенте/edge автоматически попадают в дашборд с PII-скрабом; внешний uptime-монитор бьёт тревогу при падении /api/health (включая деградацию БД, не только процесса); /api/metrics отдаёт насыщение pg-пула, глубину/возраст tg_outbox (включая dead-letter), глубину очереди верификации и 5xx-счётчик; алерт в Telegram срабатывает при: (a) сбое cron (housekeeping/tg-outbox) через внешний dead-man's-switch, (b) tg_outbox backlog age > порога. Закрывает Кластер G (launch-readiness §2) и часть Кластера F/C3 (cron-надёжность).

OBS-1 (Sentry) и OBS-9 (CSP tunnel) должны идти вместе — иначе client-side ошибки тихо блокируются CSP connect-src 'self' и acceptance-критерий 'ошибка попадает в дашборд' не выполняется для браузерной половины. OBS-7/OBS-8 (алертинг) зависят от OBS-4 и переиспользуют src/lib/telegram/notify.ts как транспорт — Prometheus/Grafana не планируется, потребителя метрик нет. Рекомендованный порядок: OBS-2 → OBS-6 → OBS-1+OBS-9 (параллельно) → OBS-4 → OBS-3, OBS-5, OBS-7, OBS-8 (параллельно после OBS-4).

tasks.title: Health-check: честный HTTP-статус вместо ok:true всегда
tasks.what: src/app/api/health/route.ts:20 возвращает NextResponse.json({ok:true, db, ts}) с HTTP 200 ВСЕГДА, даже когда db===false (DB down). Метрики пула — не сюда (см. OBS-4), health должен остаться дешёвым (Railway healthcheckPath дёргает его часто).

tasks.risk: railway.json healthcheckTimeout=120 + restartPolicyMaxRetries=5 — 503 из-за временной недоступности БД (напр. failover) теперь активно триггерит рестарт здорового веб-процесса; согласовать с инфра-воркстримом, не гасить restart policy молча.

Добавить в ответ route dead_letter_count (COUNT WHERE attempts>=5 AND sent_at IS NULL) — нужен для OBS-4/OBS-7. housekeeping/route.ts уже возвращает 207 при частичном отказе — verify, не менять.

tasks.title: Secret-protected /api/metrics: pg-pool, tg_outbox depth/age/dead-letter, verification queue depth, 5xx rate
tasks.what: Новый роут GET /api/metrics, защищённый тем же паттерном что cron-роуты (X-Cron-Secret либо отдельный METRICS_SECRET в env.ts). JSON-ответ (не Prometheus text-format — скрейпера в стеке нет): (1) pg pool — pool().totalCount/idleCount/waitingCount из node-pg Pool (src/lib/pool.ts), насыщение = totalCount-idleCount относительно PG_POOL_MAX; (2) tg_outbox — COUNT WHERE sent_at IS NULL (depth), MAX(now()-created_at) WHERE sent_at IS NULL (oldest pending age сек), COUNT WHERE attempts>=5 AND sent_at IS NULL (dead-letter, из OBS-6); (3) verification queue depth — COUNT FROM verification_cases WHERE state<>'closed' (тот же источник истины, что рекомендован в launch-readiness Кластер C для дашборд-счётчика); (4) 5xx rate — читает агрегат из OBS-5.
tasks.acceptance: GET /api/metrics без секрета → 401/503; с валидным секретом → 200 JSON со всеми полями (pool_total, pool_idle, pool_waiting, outbox_depth, outbox_oldest_age_seconds, outbox_dead_letter_count, verification_queue_depth, five_xx_rate_5min); проверено вручную вставкой тестовой pending outbox-записи с created_at в прошлом — outbox_oldest_age_seconds отражает реальный возраст.

tasks.title: 5xx rate: rolling-window счётчик через onRequestError или lightweight in-memory counter
tasks.what: Единственный веб-инстанс (реплики архитектурно невозможны — single-attach volume) — in-memory counter безопасен, Redis не нужен для MVP. Реализовать rolling-window счётчик 5xx-ответов (bucket по минутам за последние 5 мин), инкрементируемый из onRequestError-хука в instrumentation.ts (ловит неперехваченные ошибки Route Handlers/Server Components) — но НЕ явные NextResponse.json(...,{status:5xx}) без throw, те роуты нужно инкрементировать вручную или через обёртку в src/proxy.ts (прочитать файл перед реализацией — определить, видит ли Routing Middleware финальный статус ответа Route Handler). Значение читает OBS-4.
tasks.acceptance: Намеренно вызвать 3 разных 5xx-ответа (напр. временно сломав DB) в течение окна — GET /api/metrics five_xx_rate_5min отражает рост; после окна (5 мин) счётчик спадает к 0 без ручного сброса.
tasks.risk: In-memory counter теряется при каждом рестарте процесса (единственный инстанс) — приемлемо для MVP-порога тревоги, задокументировать ограничение; на пост-10k этапе (R2/S3+реплики) заменить на Redis-backed.

Scope = build screens + DB + records + withdrawal + admin view; all user-facing copy is placeholder marked LAWYER_REVIEW (lawyer reviews wording in parallel). Fixes LEGAL-005, 006, 007, 008 (critical), 009, 015 from audit-mvp-vs-spec-2026-07-01.md; addresses Cluster A of launch-readiness-2026-07-02.md.

LC-7 (withdrawal) depends on LC-1+LC-2. LC-8 (admin legal view) depends on LC-1. LC-9 (restart wipe verify) depends only on LC-1. Migration filenames must sort AFTER 20260701010000_anketa_v4_enum_values.sql — use 20260702xxxxxx prefixes. NB: despite the supabase/ dir name, storage is native pg + Railway Volume; treat SQL files as plain migrations, no Supabase-specific tooling.

Withdrawal semantics: confirm that withdrawing sensitive-PD consent should (a) only flip consent status to 'withdrawn' and stop future processing, or (b) also purge/anonymize the already-collected sensitive fields (extended.finance/lifestyle). Plan implements (a) status-flip + audit now; (b) purge is flagged as a follow-up tied to the LEGAL-023/024 retention-matrix workstream, not this P0.

Where the sensitive-consent gate sits relative to profile_family_model: plan inserts it immediately before profile_finance (first sensitive screen). tasks.title: Migration: enrich consents table with status/source/action_id/category + status enum + backfill

tasks.title: Server helper: recordConsentMiniApp() with full proof capture
tasks.what: Create a server-only helper mirroring bot handlers.ts recordConsent() but for the mini-app, capturing real proof instead of hardcoded constants. Signature: recordConsentMiniApp({ userId, telegramId, types, categories?, text, lang, ip, userAgent, source }) → returns action_id. Writes consents rows with consent_status='active', source (default 'mini_app'), generated action_id, categories (for sensitive), telegram_id, ip, user_agent, language, consent_text_sha256 = sha256(text + '::' + LEGAL_VERSION). Idempotent upsert on (user_id,consent_type,consent_version) ignoreDuplicates. Caller extracts real ip/user_agent from request headers. Reuse LEGAL_VERSION from @/content/legal.
tasks.acceptance: Integration: calling with types=['sensitive'], categories=['finance','lifestyle'] inserts one row with consent_status='active', source='mini_app', non-null action_id, categories={finance,lifestyle}, telegram_id set, consent_text_sha256 = sha256(text+'::'+LEGAL_VERSION). Second identical call does not duplicate. ip/user_agent reflect passed request values, not 'tg-webhook'.

plans.goal: Ship revenue-from-day-1: Plus (149 000 сум/мес) gates chat after mutual interest. A verified user with an active Plus/Pro subscription (or whose pair-partner has one) can open the chat and message; everyone else sees a paywall instead of the composer. Both Click and Payme webhooks activate the subscription idempotently (replay-safe), atomically grant Plus, unlock the locked chat, and emit analytics. Plan limits (pending requests, active acquaintances) are enforced per plan. Subscription expiry downgrades to free via cron; mutual-interest lock expires after 7 days via cron. Chat gating is a pair-level chat_status property, kept orthogonal to the existing Role/Permission matrix. Source of truth: subscriptions table; users.base_plan + plan_expires_at are denormalized for cheap reads.
plans.sequencing_note: DB layer first (REV-1 schema, REV-2 grant/downgrade/limit RPCs) — everything depends on it. Then wire mutual-interest lock into process_interest (REV-3) and the chat chokepoints (REV-4 loadChatRow + API routes, REV-5 chat detail page + paywall UI). Payment plumbing (REV-6 env, REV-7 payment_sessions + create-session route, REV-8 Click webhook, REV-9 Payme webhook) can proceed in parallel with the gating work once REV-1/REV-2 land, but all webhooks call the REV-2 grant RPC so they depend on it. Tariff/paywall screens (REV-10, REV-11) depend on REV-7 for the create-session call. Limit enforcement (REV-12) depends on REV-2 counters + REV-3. Analytics (REV-13) is a thin dependency used by webhooks and UI. Cron sweeps (REV-14) depend on REV-2 downgrade RPC and REV-3 lock. Admin read-only view (REV-15) last. Acceptance gates: (a) sandbox Click OR Payme test payment flips payment_sessions→paid, base_plan→plus, chat_status locked→open in one atomic RPC; (b) re-POSTing the same webhook payload is a no-op (idempotent); (c) cron with plan_expires_at in the past downgrades base_plan→free and re-applies free limits without re-locking already-open chats.
open_decisions: Either-party vs both-party unlock: face-value reading of Экран 2/3 (Free user sees 'подключите Plus'; after payment chat opens) and the pair-level chat_status field imply EITHER party's active Plus unlocks the pair (payer unlocks for both). Recommended default = either-party unlock. Has a free-rider revenue implication — confirm with founder. Plan is written to this default; flip is a one-line change in the grant RPC + process_interest lock predicate.

Chat fate on subscription expiry (spec §24-q12, unresolved): recommended MVP = grandfather already-open chats (do NOT retroactively re-lock — hostile UX), downgrade only limits/new-chat gating. REV-14 built to this. Confirm with founder.
Mutual-interest 7-day retention (spec §Экран2 'confirm with owner'): recommended mutual_interest_retention_days=7, lock→expired via cron. Configurable constant.

Pro price not finalized (spec offers 249k/299k/399k). MVP SKU is Plus 149 000 only; Pro screen/SKU is built as data-driven (price from a plan-catalog constant) so the number can be set later without code changes. Pro purchase is in scope structurally but the single required MVP SKU is Plus.
Gifting (Экран 7) is explicitly out of MVP per locked decisions and spec §22-23 (gift = next stage). Not planned here; payment_sessions.kind carries a 'gift' value reserved but unused.

'Active acquaintance' (active_connection) definition for slot accounting: recommended = an open chat row (chat_status='open') that is not closed/blocked. There is no chat-close feature in the current codebase, so Plus active_connection_limit=1 effectively means 'first mutual unlocks, second mutual with no Plus upgrade shows active-connection-limit paywall'. A 'finish acquaintance' action (to free a slot) is noted as a follow-up dependency, not built in this workstream.

tasks.title: Grant/downgrade/limit-counter RPCs (SECURITY DEFINER, idempotent grant)
tasks.what: PL/pgSQL functions mirroring the process_interest pattern (advisory lock + status-transition replay guard). (1) grant_plan(p_session uuid) returns table(result text, chat_id uuid): takes advisory lock on the session; if payment_sessions.status already 'paid' → return ('already_granted', chat_id) (idempotent no-op); else set status='paid', insert/extend subscriptions row (active, expires_at = now()+duration), set users.base_plan + plan_expires_at, and if session.chat_id is set and that chat.status='locked_requires_plus' → set chat.status='open' (either-party unlock: the payer unlocking their own locked pair). Return ('granted', chat_id). (2) expire_subscriptions() returns int: for users where plan_expires_at < now() and base_plan<>'free' → base_plan='free', mark subscriptions expired; returns count. Does NOT re-lock open chats (grandfather). (3) count_pending_interests(p_user uuid) returns int and count_active_connections(p_user uuid) returns int — helpers for limit checks (pending = match_requests where sender=user, status='pending', auto_decline_at>now(); active = chats where user is a party and status='open'). (4) plan_limits(p_plan plan_tier) returns table(pending_limit int, active_limit int) — SQL constant map (free 2/0, plus 3/1, pro 5/2). Register grant_plan, count_* , plan_limits set-returning fns in SET_RETURNING array.
tasks.acceptance: Calling grant_plan twice with the same session id activates the plan once and returns 'already_granted' the second time (verified by row counts). expire_subscriptions() flips an over-due user to free and leaves an already-open chat status='open'. plan_limits('plus') returns (3,1). SET_RETURNING contains the new set-returning fn names so .rpc() returns arrays.

tasks.title: Click webhook: Prepare + Complete, signature verify, idempotent grant
tasks.what: POST /api/payments/click/webhook implementing Click Merchant API two-phase callback (action=0 Prepare, action=1 Complete). Verify the MD5 sign_string per the Click Merchant API contract (concatenation of click_trans_id, service_id, SECRET_KEY, merchant_trans_id, [merchant_prepare_id on Complete], amount, action, sign_time) using safe-equal (src/lib/crypto/safe-equal.ts). Map merchant_trans_id → payment_sessions.id, validate amount matches the session, set provider_txn_id=click_trans_id. On successful Complete → call grant_plan(session.id) RPC (idempotent), then emit analytics 'payment_success' + 'chat_unlocked' (if a chat was unlocked) and enqueue an outbox 'chat_unlocked' notify to the payer. Respond with Click's required JSON envelope (click_trans_id, merchant_trans_id, merchant_confirm_id, error, error_note) with correct error codes (-1 sign check failed, -4 already paid, -5 user/order not found, -9 transaction cancelled, 0 success). Guard: return 'provider_not_configured' if REV-6 vars unset.
tasks.acceptance: A signed sandbox Click Prepare+Complete sequence flips the session to 'paid', activates Plus, unlocks the linked chat (status→open), and re-POSTing the same Complete returns Click's 'already paid' code without double-granting. A wrong signature is rejected (-1). ACCEPTANCE also requires: 'verify the exact sign_string field order + error-code set against current Click Merchant API v2 docs before shipping' (do not trust a from-memory formula).
tasks.db_changes: Reads/writes payment_sessions; calls grant_plan RPC.
tasks.risk: Signature field order and the JSON response envelope are Click-specific and easy to get wrong from memory — treat the doc as source of truth (acceptance line). Idempotency comes from grant_plan's status guard + unique (provider, provider_txn_id).

tasks.title: Payme webhook: JSON-RPC Merchant API, Basic-auth verify, idempotent grant

Implement methods: CheckPerformTransaction (validate order/session exists, state pending, amount matches → allow), CreateTransaction (record provider_txn_id=params.id, state), PerformTransaction (→ call grant_plan(session.id), emit analytics 'payment_success'+'chat_unlocked', return perform_time+state), CancelTransaction (mark session failed/cancelled; if already performed handle reversal state per Payme rules), CheckTransaction (return current state/times), GetStatement (optional). Guard: 'provider_not_configured' if vars unset.

ALL OTHER filters are invariant across every level and must be re-verified unchanged at each level: `c.lifecycle_state='active'`, `c.verification_status='approved'`, viewer-gate (u.lifecycle_state='active' and u.verification_status='approved'), `cp.status='published'`, mutual gender match (`cp.gender=v.looking_for_gender` and `v.gender=cp.looking_for_gender`), has-approved-photo exists-clause, match_views dedup, blocks exclusion, match_requests pending/accepted/auto_decline exclusion.
